snp4.4:1.1:
“I see the pure, the supreme,
free from disease.
snp4.4:1.2:
It’s in connection
with what’s seen
that a person’s purity
is.”
snp4.4:1.4:
& remaining focused
on purity,
one falls back on that knowledge.
snp4.4:2.1:
If it’s in connection
with what is seen
that a person’s purity is,
snp4.4:2.2:
or if stress is abandoned
in connection with knowledge,
snp4.4:2.3:
then a person with acquisitions
is purified
in connection with something else,
snp4.4:2.4:
for his view betrays that
in the way he asserts it.
snp4.4:3.1:
No brahman
says purity
comes in connection
with anything else.
snp4.4:3.2:
Unsmeared with regard
to what’s seen, heard, sensed,
habits or practices,
snp4.4:3.4:
not creating
anything here,
he’s let go
of what he’d embraced.
snp4.4:4.1:
Abandoning what’s first,
they depend on what’s next.
snp4.4:4.2:
Following perturbation,
they don’t cross over the bond.
snp4.4:4.4:
—like a monkey releasing a branch
to seize at another—
snp4.4:5.1: a person undertaking practices on his own,
snp4.4:5.2:
goes high & low,
latched onto perception.
snp4.4:5.3:
But having clearly known
through vedas, having encountered
the Dhamma,
snp4.4:5.4:
one deeply discerning
doesn’t go
high & low.
snp4.4:6.1:
He’s enemy-free
with regard to all things
snp4.4:6.3:
By whom, with what,
should he
be pigeonholed
here in the world?
snp4.4:6.4:
—one who has seen in this way,
who goes around
open.
snp4.4:7.3: Untying the tied-up knot of grasping,
snp4.4:7.4:
they don’t form a desire
anywhere in the world.
snp4.4:8.2:
has nothing that
—on knowing or seeing—
he’s grasped.
snp4.4:8.3:
Unimpassionate for passion,
not impassioned for dis-,
snp4.4:8.4:
he has nothing here
that he’s grasped as supreme.
